//: What an international school teacher earns, by country. Used when neither the school nor its adverts publish a figure.
//why: Per-school salary is not public data. A sweep of job packs, school sites, aggregators and forums found figures for 9 of 521 schools. Country figures are the honest alternative: they say what to expect in a place, and they say that is what they are.
//limits: A country figure is identical for every school in that country, so it CANNOT rank schools against each other. Within-country ranking stays on package terms and accreditation. See README.
//savings: What teachers actually keep after rent and tax. Usually the more useful number: Bangkok on $38k out-saves Singapore on $55k, because Singapore rent eats the difference. Housing provision alone moves net savings by $10k-$20k a year.
//basis: reported = aggregated from teacher submissions, with a count. sourced = taken from named published figures for that country, with no submission count behind it.
//minReports: A 'reported' figure standing on fewer than 5 submissions is kept for reference but not shown: one teacher's contract is not a country average. Bangladesh sat at $88K on a single report.
//currency: USD per year, gross base salary, excluding housing, flights and dependant places. The Package columns carry those.

Singapore.crosscheck: isc: $55k-$90k — our average sits at the top of their range, so treat it as the ceiling rather than the middle

Peru.crosscheck: a Lima posting at EUR 3,000-3,400/mo is nearer $39k-$44k, so this average may be high

countries.//sourced: No submission pool, but named published figures exist for the country. Shown, and labelled as sourced rather than reported.

Costa Rica.note: International school posting at $2,400-$2,600/mo, plus the legally mandated 13th-month aguinaldo.

Papua New Guinea.note: PGK 70,000-100,000 a year, converted at roughly 0.27 USD.

Australia.note: AUD 91,500-110,000 at about 0.66 USD. Local scale: schools here recruit domestically, so there is no expat premium, no housing and no flights — read the Package columns as mostly empty by design rather than unknown.
Australia.crosscheck: two teacher submissions put it at $83k, above this range; those are likely senior or leadership posts

New Zealand.note: NZD 62,000-98,000 in Auckland at about 0.60 USD. Local scale, as in Australia.

countries.//thin: Reported, but below the threshold. Kept so the gap is visible and a later run can top them up; not shown.
countries.//missing: Searched and not found for international-school expat pay: Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Kyrgyzstan, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Maldives and the smaller islands. PayScale and Glassdoor do carry figures for several — Glassdoor puts a Kathmandu teacher at USD 41,667 and Colombo at USD 42,708 — but the same pages show actual Nepali teacher pay at NPR 25,000-35,000 a month, so those aggregates are artefacts, not salaries. Nothing is better than a wrong number.
